"'''Hot Stuff'''" is a song written by [[Pete Bellotte]], [[Harold Faltermeyer]], and [[Keith Forsey]], released as the [[lead single]] from American singer [[Donna Summer]]'s seventh studio album, '' [[Bad Girls (Donna Summer album)|Bad Girls]]''. The song was produced by English producer [[Pete Bellotte]] and Italian producer [[Giorgio Moroder]], and it was released in 1979 through [[Casablanca Records]]. Up to that point, Summer had mainly been associated with [[disco]] songs but this song also showed a significant rock direction, including a guitar solo by ex-[[The Doobie Brothers|Doobie Brother]] and [[Steely Dan]] guitarist [[Jeff Baxter|Jeff "Skunk" Baxter]]. It is the second of four songs by Summer to reach number one on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]].<ref>{{cite magazine|first= Keith |last= Caulfield |title= Donna Summer's Top 20 Billboard Chart Hits |magazine= [[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] |date= May 17, 2012 |access-date= June 13, 2014 |url= http://www.billboard.com/articles/list/488345/donna-summers-top-20-billboard-chart-hits}}</ref>

In 2018, a remix by [[Ralphi Rosario]] and Erick Ibiza entitled "Hot Stuff 2018" went to number one on the US Dance Club Songs chart.<ref>{{cite magazine|title= Dance Club Songs |magazine= [[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] |date= June 30, 2018 |access-date= June 26, 2018 |url= https://www.billboard.com/charts/dance-club-play-songs/2018-06-30}}</ref>

"Hot Stuff" is a song written by Pete Bellotte, Harold Faltermeyer, and Keith Forsey, released as the lead single from American singer Donna Summer's seventh studio album,  Bad Girls. The song was produced by English producer Pete Bellotte and Italian producer Giorgio Moroder, and it was released in 1979 through Casablanca Records. Up to that point, Summer had mainly been associated with disco songs but this song also showed a significant rock direction, including a guitar solo by ex-Doobie Brother and Steely Dan guitarist Jeff "Skunk" Baxter. It is the second of four songs by Summer to reach number one on the Billboard Hot 100.

In 2018, a remix by Ralphi Rosario and Erick Ibiza entitled "Hot Stuff 2018" went to number one on the US Dance Club Songs chart.

sections.heading: Reception
sections.wikitext: ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' claimed that "Hot Stuff" has a "strong [[rhythm and blues|R&B]], [[soul music|soulish]] feel" along with a "fiery" vocal performance from Summer.<ref>{{cite magazine|title= Billboard's Top Single Picks |magazine= [[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] |page= 73 |date= April 14, 1979 |access-date= July 8, 2020 |url= https://worldradiohistory.com/Archive-Billboard/70s/1979/Billboard%201979-04-14.pdf}}</ref>  ''[[Cash Box]]'' said that the song "has an exciting newness to its rock/disco sound" with "[[power chord|power guitar chording]], interesting synthesizer lines and unusual Summer vocal."<ref name=cb>{{cite news|title=CashBox Singles Reviews|date=April 14, 1978|page=17|newspaper=Cash Box|accessdate=January 1, 2022|url=https://worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Cash-Box/70s/1979/CB-1979-04-14.pdf}}</ref> ''[[Record World]]'' called it a "splendid rock disco tune."<ref name=rw>{{cite magazine|magazine=Record World|date=April 14, 1979|accessdate=February 11, 2023|title=Hits of the Week|page=1|url=https://worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Record-World/70s/79/RW-1979-04-14.pdf}}</ref>
sections.text: Billboard claimed that "Hot Stuff" has a "strong R&B, soulish feel" along with a "fiery" vocal performance from Summer.  Cash Box said that the song "has an exciting newness to its rock/disco sound" with "power guitar chording, interesting synthesizer lines and unusual Summer vocal." Record World called it a "splendid rock disco tune."

sections.heading: Awards and legacy
sections.wikitext:
"Hot Stuff" won Summer the [[Grammy Award]] for [[Grammy Award for Best Female Rock Vocal Performance|Best Female Rock Vocal Performance]] in the inaugural year the award was given out.

In 2010, the song was ranked No. 104 on ''Rolling Stone''{{'}}s list of "[[Rolling Stone's 500 Greatest Songs of All Time|The 500 Greatest Songs of All Time]]".<ref>{{cite web|title= 500 Greatest Songs of All Time – 104 Donna Summer, 'Hot Stuff' |magazine= [[Rolling Stone]] |date= December 11, 2003 |access-date= July 7, 2014 |url= https://www.rollingstone.com/music/lists/the-500-greatest-songs-of-all-time-20110407/donna-summer-hot-stuff-20110526}}</ref>

On September 18, 2020, Norwegian DJ Kygo released a remixed version of the song. It marks Kygo's third remix, released as a single, following "Higher Love" (2019), and "What's Love Got to Do with It (song)" (2020).

sections.heading: Background
sections.wikitext: In a press release, Kygo noted that Summer was one of his favorite artists of all time because of her brilliant catalogue and unmatched vocals. He hoped that this version would continue to bring the joy that the original track did.<ref name="Kygo"/>
sections.text: In a press release, Kygo noted that Summer was one of his favorite artists of all time because of her brilliant catalogue and unmatched vocals. He hoped that this version would continue to bring the joy that the original track did.

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext: A music video to accompany the release of "Hot Stuff" was first released onto [[YouTube]] on September 17, 2020.<ref>{{cite web|title= Kygo, Donna Summer – Hot Stuff (Official Video) |publisher= [[YouTube]] |date= September 17, 2020 |access-date= September 28, 2020 |url= https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yg6Y_1_DJyI}}</ref> The video is directed by Bo Webb, starring ''[[Outer Banks (TV series)|Outer Banks]]'' cast members [[Madelyn Cline]] and [[Chase Stokes]]. The music video details a blossoming love between the two as they dance the night away amidst blue and purple hues.<ref>{{cite news|title= Kygo Unveils Remix of Donna Summer's Legendary "Hot Stuff" Alongside Music Video |newspaper= Edm.com - the Latest Electronic Dance Music News, Reviews & Artists |date= September 18, 2020 |access-date= October 6, 2020 |url= https://edm.com/music-releases/kygo-donna-summers-hot-stuff}}</ref>

sections.heading: Appearances in other media
sections.wikitext:
*Professional wrestler [[Eddie Gilbert (wrestler)|"Hot Stuff" Eddie Gilbert]] took his [[ring name]] from the song, which he also used as his entrance theme.<ref>{{cite web|author= official.streetsmarks |title= Extreme Retro Review #001: ECW/WWA Battle of the Belts 01.23.93 |website= Inside Pulse |date= January 28, 2019 |access-date= October 15, 2019 |url= https://insidepulse.com/2019/01/28/extreme-retro-review-001-ecw-wwa-battle-of-the-belts-01-23-93/}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first= Ryan |last= Nation |title= All in the family: The Gilberts story |website= [[Canoe.com|Slam!]] |date= April 15, 2011 |access-date= October 15, 2019 |url= http://slam.canoe.com/Slam/Wrestling/2011/04/15/18013386.html|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20151201193351/http://slam.canoe.com/Slam/Wrestling/2011/04/15/18013386.html|url-status= dead|archive-date= December 1, 2015}}</ref>
*The song was used in the 1997 film ''[[The Full Monty]]''. During a press event on his 50th birthday, [[Charles III|Charles, Prince of Wales]] helped recreate the scene in which the four main characters overhear the song while waiting in line at the unemployment office.<ref>{{cite news|title= The Full Monarchy |publisher= [[BBC News]] |date= November 13, 1998 |access-date= April 14, 2008 |url= https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/213847.stm}}</ref>
*The song is featured in the 2015 film ''[[The Martian (film)|The Martian]],'' during a scene in which [[Matt Damon]]'s character uses radioactive material to keep warm whilst stranded on [[Mars]].<ref>{{cite magazine|first= Melinda |last= Newman |title= The Martian Soundtrack Filled with Disco Classics |magazine= Billboard |date= October 2, 2015 |access-date= October 11, 2015 |url= https://www.billboard.com/music/pop/the-martian-soundtrack-disco-music-guardians-of-the-galaxy-6715353/}}</ref>
*[[Mexico|Mexican]] pop star [[Lorena Herrera]] covered the song in [[Spanish language|Spanish]] renaming it "Algo prendido".
*The song is playable in the 2010 game ''[[Just Dance 2]]''<ref>{{cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QeyyFTOxthk |title=Just Dance 2 Gameplay - Hot Stuff |author=Just Dance |date=August 13, 2010 |access-date=January 27, 2025 |via=[[YouTube]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.eurogamer.net/mj-just-dance-2-tracklists-outed|title=MJ, Just Dance 2 tracklists outed|date=August 18, 2010 | work=[[Eurogamer]] | first=Robert | last=Purchese}}</ref> and the 2011 game ''[[Dance Central 2]]''.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.eurogamer.net/dance-central-2-tracklist-expands|title=Dance Central 2 tracklist expands|date=August 16, 2011 | first=Fred | last=Dutton | work=[[Eurogamer]] }}</ref>
*It is heard in multiple commercials.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://adage.com/article/adages/a-back-donna-summer-s-long-commercial-career/234832|title=A Look Back at Donna Summer's Long Commercial Career|work=[[Ad Age]] | first=Shareen | last=Pathak | date=May 17, 2012 | url-access=subscription | quote="Hot Stuff" was another marketer favorite. That track appeared in a 1979 commercial in Australia for Four'n Twenty Pies, as well as a 2003 Capital One spot and a 2003 Garnier Nutrisse ad. }}</ref>
*The song was used in ''[[Mafia!]]'', a 1998 American crime comedy film directed by [[Jim Abrahams]].
*The song is played at the conclusion of the [[Pop-Tarts Bowl]], a [[college football]] [[bowl game]] sponsored by [[Kellanova]], when the winning team feasts on what was advertised as an "edible mascot" as a result of winning the game.<ref>{{Citation |title=Kansas State Eats Pop-Tarts Edible Mascot After Bowl Win | date=December 28, 2023 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZZ6HoJdHslI |access-date=January 10, 2024 |language=en}}</ref>
*Dutch DJ duo, [[Vicetone]] remixed the song, released as "Hawt Stuff", on May 27, 2016.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 27, 2016 |title=Hawt Stuff - Vicetone |url=https://open.spotify.com/track/0FFy8wf7ziAwheryuiKaJP |website=Spotify}}</ref>
sections.text:
*Professional wrestler "Hot Stuff" Eddie Gilbert took his ring name from the song, which he also used as his entrance theme.
*The song was used in the 1997 film The Full Monty. During a press event on his 50th birthday, Charles, Prince of Wales helped recreate the scene in which the four main characters overhear the song while waiting in line at the unemployment office.
*The song is featured in the 2015 film The Martian, during a scene in which Matt Damon's character uses radioactive material to keep warm whilst stranded on Mars.
*Mexican pop star Lorena Herrera covered the song in Spanish renaming it "Algo prendido".
*The song is playable in the 2010 game Just Dance 2 and the 2011 game Dance Central 2.
*It is heard in multiple commercials.
*The song was used in Mafia!, a 1998 American crime comedy film directed by Jim Abrahams.
*The song is played at the conclusion of the Pop-Tarts Bowl, a college football bowl game sponsored by Kellanova, when the winning team feasts on what was advertised as an "edible mascot" as a result of winning the game.
*Dutch DJ duo, Vicetone remixed the song, released as "Hawt Stuff", on May 27, 2016.
